 National Centre of Meteorology confirms 2.3-magnitude tremor detected off Fujairah on Wednesday
 The National November 04, 2026
 Add on Google 
 A 2.3-magnitude earthquake struck off Fujairah's coast on Wednesday, detected at a depth of 5km south of Khor Fakkan at 8.06pm.
 The UAE has recorded several minor tremors in 2024, including quakes near Dibba and Masafi, indicating a pattern of low-level seismic activity.
 Earthquakes measuring five or above on the Richter scale are classified as "strong"; Wednesday's tremor falls well within the minor category.
 Seismic events are relatively uncommon in the UAE, though tremors linked to earthquakes in Iran are recorded more frequently in the region.
 The UAE's proximity to active fault lines in the Gulf and Indian Ocean region makes low-level seismic activity "an occasional occurrence rather than a significant concern."
 A minor earthquake measuring 2.3 on the Richter scale struck off the coast of Fujairah on Wednesday, the latest in a series of small tremors recorded in the emirate. 
 The UAE's National Centre of Meteorology confirmed the seismic activity was detected off Fujairah's coastline, south of Khor Fakkan, at 8.06pm at a depth of 5km. 
 The NCM monitored the tremor through its National Seismic Network, which tracks earthquake activity across the country. 
 Oman struck by minor earthquake in Madha region
 Read More Arrow It follows a 1.6-magnitude quake off the coast of Dibba on October 16. Dibba also experienced a 3.0-magnitude quake on August 18, while a 2.8 tremor hit Masafi on June 8. 
 Earthquakes are classified on a scale that designates any tremor measuring five or above as “strong”. Wednesday's quake and the October tremor fall well within the minor category, posing little risk to residents or infrastructure. 
 Seismic events are relatively uncommon in the UAE and Oman, though tremors linked to earthquakes elsewhere in the region – particularly in Iran – are recorded more frequently. 
 The UAE sits near several active fault lines in the broader Gulf and Indian Ocean region, making low-level seismic activity an occasional occurrence rather than a significant concern.
